proposal.utterance: In BFO terms, what kind of entity is an act of recognition in law?

entities.label: ActOfRecognition
entities.rationale: An act of recognition in law is a temporally extended happening — an occurrent process — in which legal officials, courts, or participants actively recognize a norm, rule, authority, or legal status. It unfolds in time and thus is a BFO Process. The existing class ActOfAcknowledgment (BFO_0000015) is the closest parent in the working ontology; ActOfRecognition is a species of acknowledgment specifically tied to legal validity-conferring or status-ascribing activity. It is distinct from SocialRecognition (also BFO_0000015) which is broader; ActOfRecognition is the particular legal episode.

relations.rationale: ActOfRecognition is a subkind of ActOfAcknowledgment: every act of legal recognition is an act of acknowledgment, but the converse need not hold.
Directly grounds ActOfRecognition in BFO Process to make the BFO typing explicit, inherited also through ActOfAcknowledgment.

open_questions: Should ActOfRecognition be further differentiated into subclasses by agent type (e.g., JudicialActOfRecognition, LegislativeActOfRecognition, OfficialActOfRecognition)?

Is the act of recognition here conceived as a singular dated event (individual) or as a recurrent kind (class)? The utterance uses 'an act of recognition', suggesting either; I have proposed a class to cover the general case.

Should ActOfRecognition be linked to the existing PatternOfRecognition (BFO_0000031) via a 'realizes' or 'instantiates' relation, since repeated acts might collectively constitute or realize a pattern?

Is the bearer of the resulting legal status (e.g., a LegalRight or CourtAuthority role) brought into existence by or realized in this process? If so, BFO_0000055 (realizes) from ActOfRecognition to the relevant realizable entity should be added.
proposal.rationale_summary: An act of recognition in law is paradigmatically a BFO Process (BFO_0000015): it is an occurrent that unfolds in time, involves one or more participants (officials, courts, legislatures, or the broader legal community), and produces or sustains a legal effect — typically conferring validity, status, or authority on a norm or institution. It is not a continuant because it does not persist through time with self-identity; it happens and then is over. It is not a specifically dependent continuant (quality or role) because it is not a property inhering in a bearer; it is the event itself. It is not a generically dependent continuant because it is not an information artifact that can be multiply instantiated by being copied. The closest existing working class is ActOfAcknowledgment (already typed as BFO_0000015), making ActOfRecognition a natural subclass. The existing SocialRecognition class (BFO_0000015) is also related but broader; ActOfRecognition in the legal sense is more specific, tied to validity-conferring functions within legal systems. PatternOfRecognition (BFO_0000031) in the working ontology captures the enduring informational pattern that individual acts of recognition collectively instantiate, so the two are complementary: acts realize the pattern.
